key_insight: Language models varied widely in medical physics calculations, and strong calculation performance did not always translate into reliable detection of others’ errors.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark tests calculations relevant to radiation delivery and safety checks, but its results do not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Ten seeded generators cover radiation therapy, diagnostic imaging, nuclear medicine and radiation protection.
Code-based reference answers are graded with unit conversion and tolerance bands.
Separate checking tasks present worksheets or final results, with half containing one planted error.
evidence_signal: Across 12 models evaluated on a held-out split of 1,200 items, with two models receiving half the split, calculation accuracy ranged from 33.3% to 100%; five models detected at least 96.7% of mostly large planted errors with at most 4% false alarms.
watch_item: Two shielding-item problems discovered after evaluation affected grading, and mostly large planted errors may not represent subtler clinical mistakes.
paper_title: MedPhysBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Language Models on Medical Physics Calculations and Error Detection
